claims.head: Watch Calgary’s puck management
claims.call: At least its usual 7.7% of Colorado’s 5-on-5 chances come right after winning the puck.
claims.body: Calgary gives up more dangerous chances after losing the puck than most (30th of 32 at avoiding breakdowns). Colorado ranks 3rd for chances off turnovers.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season

check.measure: share of 5-on-5 expected goals within 5 seconds of winning the puck
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Expect Colorado to fire from everywhere
claims.call: Colorado takes at least its usual 69.6 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: Few teams shoot as often as Colorado: 69.6 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, 1st in the league. Calgary sits 27th of 32 at keeping shots down.

claims.head: Expect a track meet
claims.call: The game runs at more than the two teams’ usual 86.9 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: Colorado’s games average 88.6 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (1st of 32 for pace); Calgary’s average 85.3 (3rd).

notes.text: M. Pospisil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 2% last season.

CGY.head: Calgary faces a real test
CGY.body: Colorado has controlled the play far better over recent games, Colorado is playing for the second night in a row, and Calgary has home ice. Calgary can pull it off if it pounces on loose pucks.

COL.head: Colorado has a lot going for it
COL.body: Colorado has controlled the play far better over recent games, Colorado is playing for the second night in a row, and Calgary has home ice. Calgary’s way back in is pouncing on loose pucks.
